items.q: Breaking bonds needs 500 kJ and forming bonds releases 650 kJ. What is ΔH for the reaction?
items.qAf: Die breek van bindings benodig 500 kJ en die vorming van bindings stel 650 kJ vry. Wat is ΔH vir die reaksie?
items.explain: ΔH = energy in (bonds broken) − energy out (bonds formed) = 500 − 650 = −150 kJ.
items.explainAf: ΔH = energie in (bindings gebreek) − energie uit (bindings gevorm) = 500 − 650 = −150 kJ.

items.q: A reaction with a negative ΔH is:
items.explain: Negative ΔH means energy is released to the surroundings.
items.explainAf: Negatiewe ΔH beteken energie word aan die omgewing vrygestel.

items.q: The enthalpy of the products is higher than that of the reactants. The reaction is:
items.qAf: Die entalpie van die produkte is hoër as dié van die reaktanse. Die reaksie is:
items.explain: Products higher in energy means energy was absorbed, so ΔH is positive.
items.explainAf: Produkte hoër in energie beteken energie is geabsorbeer, dus is ΔH positief.

items.q: Melting ice is an example of an:
items.qAf: Die smelt van ys is ’n voorbeeld van ’n:
items.explain: Heat is absorbed from the surroundings to melt the ice.
items.explainAf: Hitte word uit die omgewing geabsorbeer om die ys te smelt.

items.q: Combustion of methane releases heat, so the temperature of the surroundings:
items.qAf: Verbranding van metaan stel hitte vry, so die temperatuur van die omgewing:
items.explain: Exothermic reactions transfer heat to the surroundings.
items.explainAf: Eksotermiese reaksies dra hitte na die omgewing oor.

items.q: A cold pack used for sprains works because dissolving the salt is:
items.qAf: ’n Koue pak vir verstuiting werk omdat die oplos van die sout:
items.explain: The dissolving salt absorbs heat from the pack, making it feel cold.
items.explainAf: Die oplossende sout absorbeer hitte uit die pak, sodat dit koud voel.
